title: fixtures that write a proof file git commits write it LF, so the ladder's bound hash finds its blob on Windows
intention: The fixtures that write a proof file which git commits or a seal hashes write it with newline=LF, so the committed blob equals the bytes the ladder bound, on Windows as on Linux.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: with Path.write_text forced to newline LF (sitecustomize), test_rung_4_follows_the_ticket_kind and test_clearance.py/_accepts_a_recorded_approval/_reads_a_plan_approval went FAIL to PASS; 41 other Group H proofs stayed FAIL
traces_to: Law 3: the four greens were measured by re-running with write_text forced to LF; Law 8: a hollow revert of the four calls reds both ast teeth on Linux; Law 4: held by a scan, not remembered.
how: Add newline="\n" to the four write_text calls on `proof`: _world (two) in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_rung_4_follows_the_ticket_kind.py, and _component and _covering_proof in cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/proofs/test_clearance.py (which also reads its fixture with encoding utf-8). Red-first proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_fixtures_that_git_hashes_write_lf.py holds both with ast teeth that red on Linux.

clauses.claim: _world in the rung-4 proof writes its committed proof with newline LF at every write_text on proof, so test_rung_4_follows_the_ticket_kind passes on Windows
_component and _covering_proof in test_clearance.py write their proof with newline LF, so test_clearance.py and its two runners pass on Windows

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: with Path.write_text forced to newline LF (sitecustomize), test_rung_4_follows_the_ticket_kind and test_clearance.py/_accepts_a_recorded_approval/_reads_a_plan_approval went FAIL to PASS; 41 other Group H proofs stayed FAIL
measured.how: census3.py over the 45 Group H proofs in a copy of the tree, with and without the patch; a probe wrote a file via write_text, committed it, and git show HEAD: gave a blob whose sha256 differs from the disk bytes' (CRLF true)
